newsitem.title: UK: Outlook - Metals market to eye options, Norilsk.
newsitem.headline: Outlook - Metals market to eye options, Norilsk.

text.p: Metals markets will focus on Wednesday's LME options declaration this week and watch for more news about restive workers at Norilsk Nickel, analysts said.

Heated rallies last week put fresh option strikes in play as three months copper breached $2,400 a tonne for the first time in nine months and aluminium nearly touched $1,670, the strongest since May 1996.
After see-saw trading last week -- which saw nickel slump to $7,760 then roar up to a fresh peak of $8,180 -- players would remain cautious of more wide swings.

The market will keenly watch for developments from the huge Norilsk nickel complex, where workers over the weekend adopted a strike plan, giving management 10 days to resolve problems over salary and holiday arrears.
The strike decision followed a meeting on Saturday between management and labour representatives.
A Moscow-based spokesman for the RAO Norilsky Nickel group said he had no comment.
Last Thursday, an appeal body of three Norilsk town officials decided that an arrears repayment schedule could only be fulfilled if there was no halt to output or sales.
The resurgence of nickel cut short a mid-week correction in other metals and analysts said a chart target for copper of $2,450 was still valid.
While producers were taking advantage of the higher levels to lock in prices, funds and speculators were buying the dips down to $2,385.
In pre-market activity on Monday, copper rose about $4 from Friday's late close of to hit $2,380.
For aluminium, the next upside chart point was pegged at $1,680, the high of May 1996.
"On the upside this market needs to consolidate above $1,641 before attempting a test of $1,673 and $1,680," said chartist Harry Creates of broker AMT.
Open interest on March $1,650 call options was at 1,531 lots (38,275 tonnes), latest LME data showed.
Lead has also barrelled through to some new option levels after last week's rally.
On Friday, three months lead surged to a high of $706 after a blistering rise the previous evening, putting in play the $725 March strike level.
Latest LME data showed open interest for $725 March call options were 586 lots (14,650 tonnes) out of a total of 799 lots (19,975 tonnes) for the month.
